jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Job Summary
The Principal Program Manager, Strategic Planning & Transformation role is responsible for shaping, operationalizing, and driving Enterprise Applications strategy. This leader partners closely with senior executives and cross-functional teams to translate strategic priorities into actionable roadmaps, measurable outcomes, and sustained business impact. The role blends strategic planning, execution rigor, financial stewardship, vendor management, and change leadership across complex, matrixed environments.

Key Responsibilities
Strategy Development & Alignment
- Lead development of multi-year strategic plans aligned to enterprise priorities, operating models, and financial targets.
- Translate strategy into clear goals, success metrics, and execution roadmaps across portfolios and teams.
- Assess internal and external trends, risks, and opportunities to inform strategic decision-making.
- Develop business cases, investment strategies, and financial models to evaluate strategic opportunities, prioritize initiatives, and optimize resource allocation.

Execution & Portfolio Leadership
- Drive execution of strategic initiatives, ensuring alignment across business, technology, finance, and operations.
- Establish governance, prioritization, and performance tracking for strategic programs and investments.
- Identify dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs; recommend mitigation strategies to senior leadership.
- Partner closely with Finance to manage strategic investment portfolios, track benefits realization, monitor budgets, and ensure delivery of expected business value.
- Oversee strategic vendor and partner relationships, ensuring contract compliance, performance management, risk mitigation, and alignment to business objectives.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence
- Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, enabling data-driven decisions and alignment across stakeholders.
- Facilitate executive-level discussions, workshops, and planning forums to drive clarity and commitment.
- Communicate strategy and progress in a compelling, concise, and actionable manner.
- Provide executive leadership with recommendations that balance business outcomes, financial performance, operational capacity, and strategic risk.

- Operational Excellence & Change Leadership

- Champion disciplined planning, execution, and continuous improvement practices.
- Drive adoption of new ways of working, operating models, and governance structures.
- Support change management, communications, and capability-building to ensure sustainable outcomes.

Communication & Leadership
- Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence senior executives and guide large, distributed teams.
- Demonstrated success in stakeholder and vendor management, including contract negotiations, performance oversight, service-level management, and delivery accountability.
- Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate strategic, operational, and financial insights to diverse audiences.
- Proven ability to build alignment, drive consensus, and influence outcomes across a broad set of internal and external stakeholders.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Strategy, Engineering, Finance, or a related field (MBA or equivalent preferred).
- 10+ years of experience in strategy, management consulting, transformation, program leadership, or equivalent roles.
- Proven experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives with executive visibility.
- Strong strategic planning, analytical, problem-solving, and financial management skills, including experience developing business cases, managing budgets, forecasting investments, tracking operational spend, and measuring return on investment (ROI).
- Demonstrated financial acumen with experience evaluating investment decisions, portfolio tradeoffs, business value realization, and alignment to organizational financial objectives.
- Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and operate effectively in a matrixed organization.
- Experience managing strategic vendors and partner relationships, including contract governance, performance management, negotiations, and service delivery oversight.

Preferred Qualifications
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt and PMP or Agile/Scrum certification highly desirable. Other valuable certifications include Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, SAFe, or specific technology/platform certifications (e.g., AWS, Azure).
- Experience in enterprise technology, digital transformation, operating model redesign, or large-scale business transformation.
- Experience managing significant technology, consulting, or managed service vendor relationships and associated budgets.
- Background in healthcare, regulated industries, or large-scale enterprises.

Leadership Competencies
Strategic Thinking: Long-term, enterprise-level perspective with strong business judgment.
Influence & Collaboration: Builds alignment and commitment across diverse stakeholders.
Execution Rigor: Drives results through disciplined planning and follow-through.
Change Leadership: Leads teams through ambiguity and transformation effectively.
Financial & Business Acumen: Demonstrates strong understanding of financial drivers, investment planning, portfolio economics, vendor management, and value realization to support sound business decisions.
Vendor & Partner Leadership: Establishes productive external partnerships, holds vendors accountable to commitments, and maximizes value from strategic investments.

The Senior Manager, Segment Strategy - Generics is an analytical individual contributor role within the strategy team, supporting the development of frameworks, models, research and strategy recommendations that enable the evaluation and execution of key strategic initiatives for our Generics business within our North America Pharmaceutical Distribution (NAPD) segment. Reporting to the VP, Product Strategy & Strategic Initiatives, this position operates as a key strategic partner to our Generics organization.

Strategic Analysis & Insight

- Manage your own time and workplan effectively; know how and when to seek input; control the quality of your own work product.

Communication & Stakeholder Support

- Exposure to healthcare, generics pharmaceutical services, or distribution businesses strongly preferred; genuine interest in the economics of the pharmaceutical value chain is essential.

- Demonstrated advanced financial modeling capability — building models from a blank sheet that connect market dynamics to P&L outcomes.

- Track record of structuring ambiguous problems, executing rigorous analysis, and producing executive-ready synthesis and deliverables.

- Experience working effectively in cross-functional teams and managing multiple deliverables under time pressure.

- Structured Problem Solver: Formulates clear hypotheses and structures workstreams well with light guidance; handles complex analyses with little oversight and moves efficiently from data to insight.

Partnering with business and technology leaders, Responsible AI Owners, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Information Security, Architecture, Data, and other control functions, this role manages the full AI Use Case lifecycle across multiple related governance activities. The Lead Program Manager drives cross-functional alignment, manages program-level risks and dependencies, resolves escalated issues, and   maintains   visibility into portfolio health, decision quality, control implementation, and ongoing monitoring.

This is a hands-on program leadership role with accountability for program outcomes rather than only process administration. Success requires the autonomy to lead complex work, influence without direct authority,   establish   scalable standards, challenge inefficient ways of working, and use analytics and automation to strengthen executive decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership and Strategic Alignment

- Break down Responsible AI program   objectives   into measurable business and technology   outcomes, and   maintain a program roadmap that translates governance requirements into executable plans, milestones, deliverables, and success measures.

- Lead the end-to-end AI Use Case governance lifecycle across intake, triage, RAIB Operations quality review, RAIB and EAIC review, final decision, control implementation, and ongoing monitoring.

- Partner with program sponsors and senior stakeholders to align governance priorities, secure support, resolve high-visibility issues, and ensure the program continues to deliver enterprise value.

Governance, Risk, and Dependency Management

- Establish and   maintain   the   program   governance structure, operating cadence, decision rights, escalation paths, service-level   objectives , and delivery standards consistent with McKesson's Responsible AI Program, Responsible AI Policy, and RAIB Charter.

- Identify ,   consolidate , and manage program-level risks, issues, interdependencies, and resource constraints across governance activities; develop mitigation plans, assign accountable owners, and escalate significant risks with recommended actions.

- Lead scope, priority, and   risk   trade-off discussions with stakeholders, driving consensus while preserving policy, control, documentation, and audit requirements.

RAIB and EAIC Leadership

The role will coordinate multiple interdependent workstreams across Human Resources, hiring leaders, Facilities, Asset Management, Technology Support, Security, and other enterprise partners to ensure new hires are welcomed, equipped, connected, and productive from the outset.

This is a hands-on, highly visible role requiring strong programme leadership, executive presence, and the ability to create accountability and drive outcomes through influence in a complex, matrixed organisation. The role will establish clear governance, remove delivery barriers, and use data and colleague feedback to improve the quality, consistency, and efficiency of the new hire journey.

Main Responsibilities

• Lead a cross-functional New Hire Experience programme with multiple parallel workstreams, milestones, dependencies, and stakeholder groups.

• Create and maintain an enterprise view of the end-to-end new hire journey, from accepted offer through onboarding, initial enablement, and transition into the role.

• Drive execution, issue resolution, decision-making, and escalation in a fast-paced, people-centred environment.

• Standardise onboarding playbooks, workflows, service expectations, roles, responsibilities, and hand-offs across participating teams.

• Coordinate readiness across workspace, access, devices, equipment, systems, orientation, communications, manager preparation, and colleague support.

• Establish governance forums, delivery cadences, reporting, decision rights, escalation paths, and clear ownership of outcomes.

• Define meaningful measures of experience, readiness, timeliness, quality, and operational performance, and use insights to prioritise improvement.

• Provide senior leaders with concise, evidence-based reporting on progress, risks, decisions, outcomes, and improvement opportunities.

• Embed continuous improvement by gathering feedback from new hires, hiring managers, and delivery partners and translating findings into action.

• Promote an inclusive, accessible, and consistent experience that supports colleagues across roles, locations, and business functions.

Key Accountabilities

Programme Leadership and Execution

• Own the integrated programme plan, roadmap, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, and benefits tracking.

• Coordinate work across multiple teams without direct authority, maintaining momentum and ensuring commitments are understood and delivered.

• Identify gaps that could affect a new hire's readiness or experience and drive timely resolution with the accountable owner.

• Prepare programme updates, decision papers, executive briefings, and recommendations for governance and leadership forums.

• Balance immediate operational needs with longer-term process, service, and experience improvements.

New Hire Journey Design and Standardisation

• Assess current onboarding practices and identify variation, duplication, delays, unclear ownership, and improvement opportunities.

• Define a consistent end-to-end New Hire Experience framework, including journey stages, service standards, control points, and expected outcomes.

• Develop and maintain practical playbooks, workflows, checklists, communications, templates, and operating procedures.

• Clarify roles, responsibilities, inputs, outputs, and hand-offs across all teams involved in enabling a new colleague.

• Ensure solutions are scalable while allowing for appropriate business, role, location, and regulatory requirements.

Cross-Functional Coordination

• Partner with Human Resources and People Leaders on pre-boarding, orientation, policies, manager readiness, colleague communications, and the overall onboarding experience.

• Coordinate with Asset Management and Technology Support on device, equipment, account, application, and access readiness.

• Partner with Facilities, Security, and relevant site teams on workspace, building access, badges, and location-specific readiness where applicable.

• Engage business, technology, procurement, learning, and other partners where their services form part of the new hire journey.

• Maintain a clear accountability model so each stakeholder understands deliverables, timing, dependencies, and escalation expectations.

Governance, Measurement and Continuous Improvement

• Establish appropriate governance, meeting cadences, working groups, decision logs, and escalation routes.

• Define and monitor measures for operational readiness, cycle time, service quality, colleague experience, issue volume, and resolution.

• Use quantitative and qualitative feedback to identify root causes, prioritise interventions, and validate whether changes improve outcomes.

• Maintain transparent reporting and ensure leaders have clear visibility of delivery status, material risks, decisions required, and realised improvements.

• Promote disciplined adoption of agreed processes and work with partners to sustain improvements over time.

Stakeholder and Executive Engagement

• Act as the central point of programme accountability for New Hire Experience outcomes.

• Build productive relationships with senior leaders, functional owners, hiring managers, and delivery teams across the organisation.

• Lead discussions, resolve conflicting priorities, and escalate material issues with clarity, judgement, and appropriate urgency.

• Communicate complex information in a concise, audience-appropriate manner and translate decisions into clear actions and ownership.

Required Skills and Experience

• 4 + years of programme or project management experience in large, complex enterprise environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading enterprise onboarding, employee experience, service delivery, operational transformation, or another complex people-centred programme.

• Proven ability to manage cross-functional programmes, dependencies, and outcomes without direct authority.

• Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, facilitate decisions, and navigate competing priorities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive reporting and presentation development.

• Strong organisational, analytical, problem-solving, and risk-management capabilities.

• Experience defining governance, operating models, process documentation, service measures, and continuous-improvement plans.

• Ability to work independently, demonstrate sound judgement, and deliver measurable outcomes in an evolving environment.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools used for collaboration, planning, analysis, reporting, and communication.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

• Programme or project management certification.

• Change management, Lean, Six Sigma, service management, or operational excellence experience.

• Experience supporting graduate, rotational, early-career, or high-volume onboarding programmes.

• Experience working within healthcare, technology, financial services, or another large, regulated multinational organisation.

• Experience using employee feedback, operational data, and service metrics to improve colleague journeys and business outcomes.

Behavioural Competencies

Programme Leadership: Creates clarity, structure, pace, and accountability across complex, interdependent work.

Customer and Colleague Focus: Designs solutions around the needs of new hires, hiring managers, and service partners.

Influence: Builds alignment and drives decisions through credibility, evidence, and strong stakeholder relationships.

Accountability: Takes ownership of outcomes, follows through on commitments, and addresses delivery gaps directly.

Collaboration: Connects teams and functions around shared objectives, clearly defined responsibilities, and effective hand-offs.

Continuous Improvement: Uses data, feedback, and root-cause analysis to simplify processes and improve quality, consistency, and efficiency.

Communication: Provides concise, transparent, and audience-appropriate updates, recommendations, and escalations.

Adaptability: Operates effectively amid ambiguity, changing priorities, and evolving organisational needs.

What Success Looks Like

• The end-to-end new hire journey is clearly defined, documented, and consistently executed.

• New colleagues receive the information, access, equipment, support, and connections they need at the appropriate point in their journey.

• Cross-functional teams operate with clear ownership, effective hand-offs, transparent service expectations, and timely escalation.

• Risks, delays, and recurring issues are identified early, addressed decisively, and reduced through sustainable process improvements.

• Senior leaders have clear visibility into programme progress, decisions, experience measures, operational performance, and outcomes.

A colleague's early experience shapes their connection to McKesson, confidence in the organisation, and ability to contribute effectively.
